title: Can people find contact information on Indian government websites?
summary: Contribute compute to check the 12,537 web hostnames in Data Libertarian’s November 2026 .gov.in directory. Across 100 assignments, volunteers look for a contact page, published email and postal address, and navigation links. The observations show what a visitor can find on the pages sampled and flag gaps for human review.
jurisdiction: India, including Union, state, Union Territory and local government websites
authority: The public bodies responsible for the websites listed in the Data Libertarian .gov.in directory
scope: Every hostname classified as web in the directory snapshot of 13 November 2026 appears in one assignment. This includes entries from official directories and passive sources.

GIGW quality checkpoint 10 covers contact information. Look for a Contact Us or Directory link and indicators of an email address, postal address and telephone on the landing page and one linked contact page.
On the landing page, look for an About link (quality checkpoint 9), a Help link (14) and a last-reviewed or updated date (5). Record the page URLs and observation time for follow-up.

“Not observed” means the reader did not recognise an indicator on the sampled pages. Language, image-based details or another location can explain a gap. Sites the reader could not access are reported separately.
out_of_scope: The 26 mail and other infrastructure hostnames in the source inventory, hostnames outside the snapshot, and private or sign-in-only pages.
Personal contact values, testing whether contact channels work, and formal GIGW certification.
